svg.title: How mango is built and run
svg.desc: Top: your agent system. Three boxes explain its parts. The agent has an address, a lifecycle, an inbox and a scheduler, and it can be composed of roles. Messaging sends messages to addresses and handles them by type. Scheduling runs an agent's own tasks, once or periodically, on the runtime's clock. Below the boxes, agents exchange messages; the agent box points to one of them, the scheduling box to another that runs a periodic task. An arrow hands the same agent system to one of two runtimes. Left, real time: containers exchange messages over TCP or MQTT, encoded by a codec, on wall-clock time, and the environment lives outside mango, connected by your code. Right, simulation: one simulation world advances simulated time in steps, keeps messages in process, optionally with simulated delay and loss, and contains the environment as an entity inside mango. Each part links to the step below that introduces it.

g.text: written once, runs in either runtime
